properties.setting_hint: along-strike endpoint gap; assess continuation, relay, or cartographic segmentation
properties.argument: Closing this 2.0 km gap would join two currently disconnected mapped systems (1.7 km and 0.4 km) into one 4.1 km system. NBMG INGENIOUS vector attribution: intra-FID raster/discretisation gap within multipart polyline FID=1940 ('Fish Lake Valley fault zone, Oasis section', NUM=49c, Well Constrained, SLIPSENSE=N, DIPDIRECT=Unspecified). Geometry: tip-to-tip along strike; mutual nearest tips; the tip points 15 deg off the link and 11 deg. The link strikes N11 E and 40% of the distance-weighted catalogued fault length within ~40 km lies within 20 deg of that strike (data-driven kinematic domain; no external stress model). Structural-setting label (geometry only; mapping to settings is ours): linkage/termination/step-over settings host ~25%/32% of characterised Great Basin geothermal systems (Faulds & Hinz 2015). Connectivity context: the catalogue network is near its critical connectivity (Berkowitz-style P=5.78 vs Pc 5.6-6.0 at the domain scale), where individual closures matter most, but Berkowitz et al. (2000) give ensemble statistics, not a verdict on this particular gap. Base coverage: 50% of its dots already lie within 300 m of the 0.2477 emission.  Graph value (Berkowitz et al. 2000 connectivity parameter, computed on the catalogue graph plus all 345 selected candidates with a=2.500 and D=1.566 held at their fitted values): this closure changes P by dP=+0.0059 (rank 117 of 345 by |dP|) and the largest-system share of total mapped fault length by -0.00000; the merged system would be 4.11 km long. It is a graph bridge: no other selected candidate joins these two sides, so this closure is what actually merges them. Status: validated on both 8-connected component holdout (0.293 vs 0.059 ctrl) and NBMG FID vector-trace holdout (0.100 vs 0.020 ctrl). Reviewer geometry cue only: along-strike endpoint gap; assess continuation, relay, or cartographic segmentation; this is not proof of a step-over or termination. Exclusive review class: same-FID_multipart-continuity.
